title: Frontend senior systemdesign multiteam architecture
question: Design the frontend architecture for a large product used by many teams, each owning different sections of the same app, e.g. an enterprise SaaS platform with dozens of feature areas.
idealAnswer:
Define clear module or ownership boundaries within the codebase, whether via a monorepo with well-enforced package boundaries or a micro-frontend split, so teams can work independently with minimal cross-team coordination for routine changes

Establish a shared foundation layer, design system, auth, routing shell, shared state/data-fetching conventions, owned centrally, so every team isn't reinventing or diverging on these cross-cutting concerns

Define clear contracts (APIs, component props, event interfaces) between owned areas so teams can change their internals without breaking others, versioning and deprecation policy matters here as much as it does for backend services

Build CI/CD that scales with team count, fast, isolated builds/tests per module, and a deployment strategy that doesn't require every team to coordinate a single monolithic release

Plan for performance governance across teams, a shared bundle-size budget, review process, and monitoring so one team's heavy dependency doesn't silently degrade the experience everyone else contributes to

Address the org/process layer explicitly, an architecture review or platform team, and a clear escalation path for cross-cutting decisions, since eight teams sharing one product will generate real disagreements that pure technical structure can't resolve alone
